chunks: And from him, from his father, from one who mentioned him, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), who said:

Indeed, among what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) advised Ali (peace be upon him) was: 'O Ali, do not have intercourse with your wife on the first night of the crescent moon, nor on the night of the middle (of the month), nor on the last night, for he fears for his offspring from one who does that, the madman.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'And why is that, O Messenger of God?' He said, 'Indeed, the jinn increase in visiting their wives on the first night of the crescent, and the night of the middle, and on the last night. Did you not see that the madman is struck down on the first of the month, and in its middle, and at its end?'

key_terms.أَوَّلُ لَيْلَةٍ مِنَ الْهِلَالِ: First night of the crescent moon (beginning of the lunar month)
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النِّصْفِ: Night of the middle (of the lunar month)

ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims avoid marital intercourse on the first, middle, and last nights of the lunar month?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia tradition of linking lunar phases to spiritual and physical vulnerabilities, specifically advising against marital intimacy on the first, middle, and last nights of the month to avoid jinnish influence. The reasoning connects the increased activity of jinn during these periods to the potential for mental affliction or madness in offspring, a phenomenon observable in the heightened incidence of insanity during these lunar windows.
